title: Bleeding, cut or scrape

differential.label: Scrape on the top layer of skin
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Skin scrapes are among the most common in-flight problems.

differential.label: Cut that may need closing
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Needs flight surgeon review.

differential.label: Heavy or spurting bleeding. Emergency
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Spurting blood can send droplet streams into the cabin.

differential.label: Object stuck in the body. Emergency
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Do not remove it.

differential.label: Shock or internal bleeding. Emergency
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis.

tests.title: Blood pressure, top number
tests.instruction: Take the blood pressure. Enter the top number.

tests.title: Pain score
tests.instruction: Enter a pain score from 0 to 10.

tests.title: Bleeding stopped?
tests.instruction: After pressure, note yes or no. Write down the time.

immediateSteps.title: Put on gloves
immediateSteps.instruction: Put on gloves before you touch the wound.

immediateSteps.title: Press on the wound
immediateSteps.instruction: Press a gauze pad or clean cloth hard on the wound. If nothing else is there, use your hand.

immediateSteps.title: Keep pressing
immediateSteps.instruction: Keep pressing until the bleeding stops. Do not lift the pad to check.

immediateSteps.title: If blood soaks through, add more
immediateSteps.instruction: Leave the first pad on. Put another pad on top. Keep pressing. Call the flight surgeon.

immediateSteps.title: Catch floating blood
immediateSteps.instruction: Hold a pad or towel around the wound. Wipe up any blood droplets in the air.

immediateSteps.title: If something is stuck in the body, leave it
immediateSteps.instruction: Do not pull it out. Pad around it. Tape it in place. Call the flight surgeon now.

immediateSteps.title: Eye wound: do not press
immediateSteps.instruction: Do not press on the eye. Use the eye card.

immediateSteps.title: Clean a scrape
immediateSteps.instruction: Wash a shallow scrape with soap and water. Pat it dry.

immediateSteps.title: Photograph the wound
immediateSteps.instruction: Take a photo of the wound. Take a new photo every 24 hours.

immediateSteps.title: Send the case to the flight surgeon
immediateSteps.instruction: Continue to handoff and send the case. Ask about closing the cut.

cautions: This card is not a diagnosis. It gives no doses. Do not lift the pad to check. Do not remove a stuck object. Do not press on an eye. Blood forms a dome on the wound in weightlessness, and spurting blood can float into the cabin, so catch it with pads. Use any kit item only as the flight surgeon directs.
sourceNote: Researcher card, Pulseframe Batch 2, 2026-11-15. Built from NASA IMM data, the 2001 ISS medical checklist (historical), the NASA Human Research Roadmap laceration page, Campbell et al. 1993 on bleeding in microgravity and MedlinePlus first aid. Not a current NASA procedure. Pending second-person safety review.
redFlagsLifeThreat: Bleeding does not stop with firm pressure.
An object is stuck in the body.
Signs of shock: confusion, clammy or pale skin, dizziness, fast pulse, weakness.
redFlagsCallGround: The cut may need stitches or closing.
Dirt will not come out with gentle cleaning.
Signs of infection: more pain, redness, swelling, yellow or brown fluid, fever.

timeLimits.item: Press until the bleeding stops. No source gives a fixed number of minutes.

whenGroundUnavailable.status: PARTIAL (historical rule found, no current rule)
whenGroundUnavailable.detail: The 2001 ISS laceration procedure says that in an emergency or during loss of signal the crew begins treatment, then calls the surgeon as soon as possible. No current public rule was found. Looked in: OCHMO briefs, 2001 ISS checklist, HRR laceration page.
firstAidThatNeedsNoGround: Add pads on top if blood soaks through.
Leave a stuck object in place.
Write down pulse, blood pressure and the time the bleeding stopped.
Send the case and photos as soon as the link returns.

candidateItemNotes: kit-white-bacitracin is listed for minor skin wounds in inventory.json. Gauze pads, bandages, medical tape, tissue adhesive, skin stapler and sutures are in NASA kit lists but not in inventory.json. No bleeding tourniquet was found in the 2015 kit list (the listed tourniquet is for IVs). equipmentIds lists equipment.json ids used by the tests and steps.
gaps: Gauze, bandages and tape are not in inventory.json, yet pressure needs them.
No bleeding tourniquet found in public ISS kit lists; no source on tourniquet use in flight was downloaded (Wilderness Environ Med 2023 review found but not read in full).
Raising the bleeding limb is Earth advice that depends on gravity; it is left out. No source covers it in flight.
No source gives a time to hold pressure.
